reasons: Password rules are defined here but there is no visible test.
The login message wording refers to medical email, which may not be intended.
Form rules must match server rules, which is not visible in this file.

terms.meaning: A written list of the rules a set of data must follow.
A library used to write these rules and check data against them.
An extra custom check added to a schema, such as making sure two passwords match.
A text pattern used to check character types, such as requiring a number.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup
sections.what: Brings in the validation library used to write the rules.
sections.why: All the form rules are written with this library.

sections.name: loginSchema
sections.title: Login form rules
sections.what: Requires a valid email and a password of at least eight characters. Also has a remember me option that defaults to off.
sections.why: Login checks are lighter than registration so existing users are not blocked by rules added later.
sections.watch_out: The email error text says medical email, which may confuse users with ordinary email addresses.

sections.name: registerSchema
sections.title: Registration form rules
sections.what: Requires a name of at least two characters, a valid email, a password with length and character rules, matching confirmation, and agreement to terms and health data processing. Also has two optional AI consent checkboxes.
sections.why: Health data needs explicit consent, and stronger passwords protect accounts.
sections.watch_out: The consent checks only run on the web form, so the server must enforce the same rules.

sections.name: forgotPasswordSchema
sections.title: Forgot password rules
sections.why: Prevents sending reset requests with blank or broken addresses.

sections.name: otpSchema, LoginInput, RegisterInput, ForgotPasswordInput, OtpInput
sections.title: One-time code rules and types
sections.what: Requires exactly six digits for the one-time code, and creates the TypeScript types from each schema.
sections.why: Six digit codes match the message sent to users. The types let the rest of the code know the shape of each form.
sections.watch_out: If a schema changes, the types update automatically, so screens may need changes too.

summary: Defines the rules for what a valid login, registration, forgot password, and one-time code form must contain on the web.
purpose: Checks form input before it is sent to the server, and gives matching error messages to show users. It also creates the matching TypeScript types so the code knows the form shape.
why: Stricter password rules on registration protect accounts. The rules are placed here so the same checks are used wherever the form appears.
how: Each form is a schema listing its fields and their checks. Registration requires a name, valid email, a strong password, matching confirmation, and the consent checkboxes for terms and health data. The one-time code must be six digits. Types are created from each schema.
inputs: Values typed into the login, register, forgot password, and code forms.
outputs: Either the checked values with the right types, or a list of error messages for the form to show.
risks: Login only requires eight characters, while registration requires mixed characters. This is intentional for login but must match the server. The login email message mentions medical email, which may confuse users. The consent refinement means the terms and data consent checks are enforced only on the web form, so the server must check them too.
debug: If a form rejects valid input, check the matching schema and its message. If the server rejects a password the form accepted, compare the rules with the server rules. If types do not match, check that the schema and the form use the same field names.
